folds.text: A **prompt** is simply what you type to Claude. Casual language, typos and your own style are all fine.
Writing a good prompt is like briefing a helpful new colleague. They are smart, but they do not know your situation unless you say so.

items: **What** you want: plan a trip, write an email, summarise a page.
**Context**: who it is for, and what Claude should know.
**Format**: a list, a table, short paragraphs.

folds.text: Vague: "Help me with my trip." Clear: "Plan a 3-day trip to Lisbon for two adults who love food and hate crowds. Give me a day-by-day list." Clear prompts need fewer follow-ups.

folds.prompt: Build a prompt. Tap the pieces in order: what, context, constraints, format.

parts.label: What
parts.text: Write a thank-you email to my neighbour.

parts.label: Context
parts.text: She watered my plants while I was away for a week.

parts.label: Constraints
parts.text: Keep it warm and under 100 words.

parts.label: Format
parts.text: Give me the email text only, ready to send.

folds.done: Built. Four small parts turned a vague wish into a prompt Claude can nail first time.
